### 2026-10-07 – # Log 1: Project Research and Conceptualization!

**2h**

# Log 1: Project Research and Conceptualization!

Hello! Today, I began researching PCB project ideas, aiming to find a project that had a real, impactful use, without using any advanced or time-consuming concepts. I explored ideas such as  IoT devices for smart home automation, desktop command centers for viewing time, temperature, timers, or music info, or handheld items such as PCB business cards or jewelry/watches. I weighed the pros and cons of each idea and found a few that I liked.

However, I finally decided to build a smart drink coaster! My plan is to use a temperature sensor to measure and monitor the temperature of a warm drink (probably tea or coffee) and display the temperature range the drink is in, with red, green, and blue LED's, representing hot, perfect, or cool temperature ranges, respectively.

I drew a quick sketch of the coaster to quickly visualize it:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KvD7dTJaHVfjYIigORhVQkYxq5FrUFSP/7b30109570378adb516a64b6402308736f81565d8f414771fc5963dfd9ca34fc.png)

I also used Gemini to generate some concept art for the smart coaster, to use later when designing the frame or figuring out the layout for the inner PCB and its temperature sensor and LEDs:

![Gemini_Generated_Image_b2uofjb2uofjb2uo](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KvD7dTJaHVfjYIigORhVQkYxq5FrUFSP/d715a8d3a53c50bb499775bff317dade899a92fa2533ecdde3fea6127473ffd9.jpg)

I also began putting together a basic components list so I can start designing the PCB layout soon:
- Microcontroller Unit (MCU)
- Contactless IR Temperature Sensor
- Status LEDs
- Enclosure/Base: 3D-printed matte grey/black housing with 3 front diffuser holes for the LEDs

As well as some optional parts for a battery power subsystem that I might or might not implement:
- LiPo Battery Charger IC
- 5V Boost Converter IC
- Lithium-Ion/LiPo Battery: 3.7V 500mAh flat LiPo cell
- Power Switch

I'm super excited to begin designing the actual PCB layout and diving deeper into this project!

### 2026-10-08 – # Update: The great pivot!

**3h**

# Update: The great pivot!
After spending a while researching and planning out the design for the smart coaster, I've realized that while it's a cool concept, what I really need is something a bit more useful and powerful with a greater range of capabilities. So I've decided to pivot the project! I've now decided to build a smart desk command center that displays information such as time, weather, and calendar events using an E-paper display and also has a built-in AI-powered voice assistant!

I'll be using a similar architecture to the previous project, including an ESP-32 controller, but now adding an E-Paper display, microphone/speaker, and temperature/humidity sensor. The coaster project helped me understand and learn how PCB's function and are designed, so I can now carry those skills over to this project!

I also generated some concept art for how I want this to look:

![Gemini_Generated_Image_xcpoylxcpoylxcpo](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KvD7dTJaHVfjYIigORhVQkYxq5FrUFSP/c7db96425b23dde9a4073f139bb3a585a13c03bfefbb66391b9a93df28627149.jpg)

Anyways, I'm now working on planning and designing the PCB board for this new project:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KvD7dTJaHVfjYIigORhVQkYxq5FrUFSP/05f5caeddaaebf72280a5da88365c8a52838798ed09a1d0af46319bc03e8a4c3.png)

I'm planning to also use a Raspberry Pi 4 board to allow fast and efficient audio to text conversion for the ai voice assistant, and the ESP32 for controlling the display, connecting to APIs, calculating the time, or reading sensor data.

I also set up the GitHub repository, and wrote a readme to introduce the project to others!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KvD7dTJaHVfjYIigORhVQkYxq5FrUFSP/6eace1a2d8e8e41ba6e6501ef4335464f5a733680142c3b11b9742354f23fc0a.png)

### 2026-10-09 – # Parts planning and PCB Design!

**4.23h**

# Parts planning and PCB Design!

Today I planned out most of the electrical components for the PCB and also began placing them into a PCB schematic on KiCad! It was difficult finding the proper components and ensuring they fulfilled what I require, but I now have most of them found.

The only component still missing is the actual E-Paper display. I've browsed numerous types online but am still unsure of the size, color range, or refresh rate I need. I'll research it deeper tomorrow and actually to choose one to add it to the design.

Also, I've decided to not include the Raspberry Pi board inside of the device itself, but rather I'll keep it running elsewhere in the house as a local server that the ESP32 microcontroller in the device can connect to. I'm hoping this dual setup will allow me to have a slim and efficient design for the smart device itself while still allowing it to efficiently translate audio to text for the voice assistant.

Here is a spreadsheet of the parts I'm using, which was created with the help of Gemini:

### 2026-10-11 – # Bill of Materials, Finalized Schematic, & Nearly Finished PCB!!

**13h**

# Bill of Materials, Finalized Schematic, & Nearly Finished PCB!!

Today has been a very busy day! I began by attempting to fully finalize my list of components/materials and add it to a spreadsheet, along with the exact part numbers and links to where I planned to buy them. I originally thought this would be quick but soon realized that finding components that fulfilled my goals while still fitting on the PCB and in my budget was much more difficult than I originally thought.

I started off by using DigiKey, Mouser Electronics, Waveshare, and Adafruit to pinpoint the exact parts I planned to use. For the microcontroller, I settled on the ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1-N32R16V. My research found that this model is easy to work with for beginners and contains enough power and RAM to efficiently run what I require, mainly a local ai model for wake word detection for the voice assistant as well as quick audio streaming for the full response to questions. Then, I began researching how E-Paper displays function and the differences present between different types. I decided that I wanted a quick refresh rate below about 2 seconds as well as the option for split-second partial refreshes. This is important because E-Paper displays function differently than regular displays: E-Paper displays need time to refresh the screen to show a new image, which can be annoying to look at if it happens too often. Overall, I ended up choosing a 4.2" E-Paper display by Waveshare, which features quick refresh times and was cheap enough to fit in my limited budget.

### 2026-10-11 – # Finalized PCB Design + Code!

**6.5h**

# Finalized PCB Design + Code!

Today I finished routing the whole PCB board! I began by remapping certain pins to ones that were more readily accessible to facilitate routing, and then I used lots of traces and vias to finally fix the tangle of guidelines.
